sources.title: 2026 Georgia Employer's Tax Guide — updated June 2026

calculationVersions.formulaInputStatus: Archived pre-change standard-deduction and allowance table not captured in current guide

calculation.percentageFormulaForPostHb463: max(0, taxableWages - periodicStandardDeduction - dependentAllowances * periodicDependentAllowance) * 0.0499 + additionalPeriodicWithholding
calculation.missingCertificate: Use sufficient federal W-4 information when available; otherwise single with zero allowances.
calculation.tableAndFormulaDifference: Published tables use income ranges and may differ slightly from the exact percentage method.

residencyAndWorkRules.residentRule: Withhold on Georgia residents for services inside or outside Georgia, except when the other work state requires withholding.
residencyAndWorkRules.nonresidentThreshold: Withhold when more than 5% of total earned income is attributable to Georgia or more than $5,000 of wages is attributable to Georgia.

filing.lookbackPeriod: Twelve months ending June 30 of immediately preceding calendar year

frequencies.condition: $800 or less per year after approved request
$200 or less per month and more than $800 per year
More than $200 per month and no semiweekly assignment

captureWarnings: The June guide establishes a May 11 withholding-rate change but does not reproduce the archived pre-change percentage inputs; the January 1 through May 10 branch is therefore incomplete.

The income-tax changes are retroactive for annual tax purposes, while employers were instructed to keep 5.19% withholding before May 11; payroll must use payment-date versioning rather than retroactively rewriting checks.
The complete wage-bracket matrices are retained in the checksummed guide and not duplicated here.
No explicit rounding instruction was located for the percentage method.

review.requiredNextStep: Capture the archived pre-May guide and exact deductions, verify payment-date boundaries and rounding, import table boundaries, and add executable cases spanning May 10 and May 11.
